([[Atlanta]], Georgia) | college = [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2025–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 34 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team ([[2025-26 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2026]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2025 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2025]]) }} '''Meleek Aker Jones Thomas''' (born August 6, 2006) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. ==Early life and high school== Thomas was born in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]]. He moved with his family to [[Charlotte, North Carolina]], when he was ten before moving back to Pittsburgh four years later. In [[middle school]], Thomas went to school and played basketball in the [[North Hills School District]].{{cite web|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/high-school-basketball/2023/04/09/post-gazette-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-meleek-thomas-brandin-cummings-lincoln-park/stories/202304090079|title=Boys basketball co-Players of the Year: Meleek Thomas and Brandin Cummings were a potent 1-2 punch|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=April 9, 2023|access-date=October 16, 2024}} Thomas then attended [[Lincoln Park Performing Arts Charter School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.timesonline.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/04/08/meleek-thomas-lincoln-park-leopards-usa-basketball-mens-junior-national-team-minicamp-new-orleans/65348403007/|title='Meant to be there': Lincoln Park's Meleek Thomas motivated after USA Basketball minicamp|work=[[The Beaver County Times]]|date=April 8, 2022|access-date=October 16, 2024}} He averaged 23.5 points, 10.8 rebounds, 5.8 assists, and 3.3 steals per game during his junior season as Lincoln Park won its second straight PIAA state championship.{{cite web|url=https://tribhssn.triblive.com/lincoln-parks-brandin-cummings-meleek-thomas-named-2024-triblive-hssn-boys-basketball-players-of-the-year/|title=Lincoln Park's Brandin Cummings, Meleek Thomas named 2024 TribLive HSSN Boys Basketball Players of the Year|first=Chris|last=Harlan|work=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]|date=April 1, 2024|access-date=October 16, 2024}} Thomas scored 1,750 points in three years at Lincoln Park.{{cite web|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/high-school-basketball/2024/06/11/lincoln-park-meleek-thomas-overtime-elite-league-basketball/stories/202406110114|title=Basketball star Meleek Thomas leaves Lincoln Park for Overtime Elite league in Atlanta|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=June 11, 2024|access-date=October 16, 2024}} After his junior year, Thomas opted to leave Lincoln Park to join the [[Overtime Elite]] league as a non-professional player for team City Reapers in order to preserve his collegiate eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/40326937/espn-no-7-prospect-thomas-goes-elite|title=ESPN No. 7 prospect Meleek Thomas goes to Overtime Elite|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=June 11, 2024|access-date=October 16, 2024}} Thomas was a consensus five-star recruit and one of the top players in the 2025 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.timesonline.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/04/22/meleek-thomas-lincoln-park-leopards-basketball-espn-class-of-2025-recruiting-rankings-wpial-piaa/65351368007/|title=Lincoln Park's Meleek Thomas ranked No. 11 in ESPN's Class of 2025 recruiting rankings|work=[[The Beaver County Times]]|date=April 22, 2022|access-date=October 16, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2024/sep/13/arkansas-target-thomas-a-5-star-for-good-reason/|title=Arkansas target Thomas a 5-star for good reason|first=Richard|last=Davenport|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=September 13, 2024|access-date=October 16, 2024}} He committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] over offers from [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]] and [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/42336781/meleek-thomas-gives-arkansas-second-top-10-recruit-2025|title=Meleek Thomas gives Arkansas second top-10 recruit for 2025|first1=Jeff|last1=Borzello|first2=Paul|last2=Biancardi|authorlink2=Paul Biancardi|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 11, 2024|access-date=November 12, 2024}} ==College career== Thomas enrolled at the [[University of Arkansas]] in July 2025 to take part in the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Razorbacks]]' summer practices.{{cite web|url=https://www.swtimes.com/story/sports/college/sec/2025/07/14/john-caliparis-first-impressions-on-arkansas-basketball-freshmen/84588863007/|title=John Calipari's first impressions on Arkansas basketball freshmen in summer practices|first=Jackson|last=Fuller|work=[[Southwest Times Record]]|date=July 14, 2025|access-date=October 3, 2025}} He averaged 15.6 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game as a freshman on 43.5% shooting from the field. Following the season, Thomas declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Goodson |first1=Connor |title=Arkansas guard Meleek Thomas enters NBA Draft, maintains eligibility |url=https://247sports.com/article/meleek-thomas-arkansas-basketball-enters-nba-draft-maintains-eligibility-281647480/ |access-date=May 13, 2026 |work=247 Sports |date=April 13, 2026}} ==Professional career== On June 24, 2026, Thomas was selected with the 34th overall pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]] but was subsequently traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with a future second round pick for pick 29 ([[Alex Karaban]]).{{cite news |title=NBA Draft Grade for Cavaliers No. 34 Pick Meleek Thomas |url=https://www.si.com/nba/cavaliers/onsi/nba-draft-grade-for-cavaliers-no-34-pick-meleek-thomas-01kvy4v05dhs |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=June 24, 2026}} ==Personal life== Thomas's older brother, Shawndale Jones, played college basketball at [[NJIT Highlanders men's basketball|NJIT]] and [[IUP Crimson Hawks|Indiana University of Pennsylvania]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5683599/2024/08/07/meleek-thomas-college-basketball-recruiting/?redirected=1|title=What it’s like to be a top-10 basketball recruit: Gucci, autographs and
